release_history_correction.scope: Versioned releases for repositories the user owns or maintains; existing project lifecycle owner, no new GitHub skill or global standing rule.
release_history_correction.baseline: Published wrapper had current-state handoff and development history but no consolidated public version history; GitHub follow-up is scoped to issues and own PRs.

boundary_checks.case: Prepare a published release of an owned repository with an existing changelog
boundary_checks.expected: Update its existing changelog with the released changes and evidence; preserve prior entries.

boundary_checks.case: Prepare the first versioned release without a changelog
boundary_checks.expected: Create CHANGELOG.md in repository convention and record version/date and relevant release guidance.
Include its version entry, clearly label experimental status and known failures; do not turn observations into measured gains.
Keep it in development notes; no required published-release entry or publication.

boundary_checks.case: Contribute an issue or a focused PR to another project
boundary_checks.expected: Follow that project conventions; no imposed new changelog or unrelated release workflow.

boundary_checks.case: Write a release note without publication authorization
boundary_checks.expected: Prepare documentation only; do not publish.

release_history_correction.verification_level: Source and boundary inspection plus governed metadata/byte-binding/deployment checks; no fresh model behavior comparison or spontaneous-trigger claim.

instruction_changes.deviation: The user wants a reusable version-by-version changelog rule for maintained repositories; the existing project lifecycle skill did not require release history and the GitHub issue/PR workflow does not govern owned-project releases.
instruction_changes.evidence: Direct user request to write this rule in an appropriate owner, following verified absence of a full public wrapper changelog. Existing breadcrumb lifecycle and GitHub follow-up scope inspected.
instruction_changes.why_instruction: A narrow release trigger and rule in the admitted project lifecycle owner make the explicit preference available before future release publication without loading or expanding an unrelated issue/PR workflow.
instruction_changes.alternative: No change leaves the release-history omission. A project-only rule would not carry to future owned repositories. A new GitHub release skill or global standing paragraph would duplicate lifecycle ownership and add discovery overhead. Existing changelog conventions and native publication tools remain in use.
